findings.title: Source-product derivation closed in both directions
findings.claim: Alongside the literal denial of parentage, the paired focus verbs can carry a bounded denial of divine source-product derivation: neither a prior source producing the subject nor the subject producing a same-order derivative supplies the relation.
findings.mechanism: The focus forms are the carrier for the accepted B005 generation relation. The wider 19:35 connection places taking a child beside direct divine command and creation, so the source-product relation meets an independent creation boundary and changes the denial from a family status alone into a qualified origin relation.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see why the two directions matter beyond a single child claim: the ayah closes both the product position and the producing position while its plain parentage remains intact.
findings.containment: The focus verbs still plainly deny begetting and being begotten. The derivational extension is qualified and does not assert that every use of the root carries this branch; target morphology in 19:35 is not supplied.

epistemic.reason: The branch and exact focus anchors are accepted and the cross-run support is trusted, while the move from birth to general source-product derivation is an extension rather than a grammatical necessity.
